questions.question: Temporary signs in construction and work areas have what colors?
questions.explanation: Temporary signs in work zones always have orange backgrounds with black writing and symbols.

questions.question: What should you do when a person using a white cane or guide dog is crossing the street?

options.text: Stop until the person is completely away from your path.
Honk your horn as you pass them.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop until the person is completely away from your path.
questions.explanation: You must stop and let the person using a white cane or guide dog cross safely. Always give blind pedestrians the right of way.

questions.question: What should you do if your gas pedal becomes stuck?
questions.explanation: If your gas pedal sticks, shift into neutral, apply the brakes, and pull safely off the road. Then turn off the engine. If the pedal stays stuck, call for help and do not drive the car.

questions.question: What is the speed limit in a school zone during school hours?
questions.explanation: A five-sided sign means you are in a school zone. Slow down to 15 mph during school hours and when children are present. Drive with extra care around children.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: You must stop for other traffic.
Traffic is merging from another road. Create extra space for drivers to merge safely.
Traffic is merging from another road. Keep to the right.

questions.correctAnswerText: Traffic is merging from another road. Create extra space for drivers to merge safely.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that traffic is merging. Check your side and rear. Move to another lane if possible to give merging drivers a clear path.

questions.question: Each time you pass another car, what happens to the risk of collision?
questions.explanation: Each time you pass another car, the risk of collision goes up. Only pass when you are sure it is safe.

questions.question: What should you do if you miss your exit on the interstate?

options.text: Quickly cut across traffic to turn.
Make a U-turn to go back.
Continue and use the next exit.
Put your car in reverse to go back.

questions.correctAnswerText: Continue and use the next exit.
questions.explanation: Do not make a sudden turn to catch your exit. If you miss it, go to the next exit instead.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Trucks are allowed on the upcoming narrow bridge.
The bridge ahead is one-way only.
Only one car can use the bridge at a time.
The bridge may be too narrow to pass or meet a truck.

questions.correctAnswerText: The bridge may be too narrow to pass or meet a truck.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. This sign warns you that the bridge ahead may be too narrow for you to meet or pass a truck. Drive carefully.

questions.question: You are driving on a divided multilane highway and see an emergency vehicle approaching with lights or sirens. What should you do?

options.text: Ignore the signal if other lanes are open.
Slow down, move to give the vehicle a clear path, and stop.
Speed up to get out of the way.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down, move to give the vehicle a clear path, and stop.
questions.explanation: When you hear a siren or see emergency lights, slow down, clear the path, and stop. Do not try to outrun the emergency vehicle.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. This sign tells you a steep hill is coming. Slow down and shift to a lower gear to control your speed and protect your brakes.

questions.question: A distraction while driving is:

options.text: Anything that makes you take evasive action.
Anything that takes your attention away from driving.
Anything that makes you pay more attention to driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Anything that takes your attention away from driving.
questions.explanation: A distraction while driving is anything that takes your attention away from driving. Distractions can happen anytime and anywhere. Distracted driving can cause crashes that result in property damage, injury, and death.

questions.question: Before turning, you should:
questions.explanation: To turn safely, turn on your signal 3 to 4 seconds before you turn.

questions.question: Which of the following commonly causes traffic accidents?

options.text: Not paying attention to the road.
Driving too fast for the conditions.

questions.explanation: Driving too fast is a major cause of crashes. Not paying attention can cause you to hit other vehicles. Most rear-end crashes happen because drivers follow too closely.

questions.question: If an officer is directing traffic at a working traffic light, drivers should:

options.text: Watch what other cars are doing.

questions.explanation: Traffic signals help keep traffic moving and prevent crashes. Drivers, pedestrians, and cyclists must obey these signals. The only exception is when an officer is directing traffic instead.

questions.question: When approaching a railroad crossing, you should:
questions.explanation: When you see a railroad crossing sign, slow down, look for a train, and be ready to stop. If the red lights are flashing or the gate is down, stop 15 to 50 feet before the tracks. Never try to go around the gate.

questions.question: Roads are most dangerous at the start of light rain when oil and water mix and make the road slippery.
questions.explanation: Wet roads can be as dangerous as icy roads. Slow down in wet weather. You need more distance to stop and may skid on turns. Light rain is most dangerous because the water mixes with road oils that haven't washed away yet, creating a slippery film.

questions.question: When driving near a blind pedestrian with a white cane or guide dog, you should:

options.text: Slow down and be ready to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and be ready to stop.
questions.explanation: When you see a blind pedestrian with a white cane or guide dog, slow down and let them cross first. Be ready to stop to keep them safe.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that a stop sign is coming.

questions.question: When driving on slippery roads, you should:

options.text: Take turns more slowly than usual.

questions.correctAnswerText: Take turns more slowly than usual.
questions.explanation: Driving too fast on slippery roads is always dangerous, especially on turns and curves. Slow down when turning on slippery roads.

questions.question: When you see a steady yellow traffic light, you should:

options.text: Speed up to avoid a red light.
Keep driving because you have the right-of-way.
Slow down and stop, unless you are already in the intersection.
Watch what other cars are doing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and stop, unless you are already in the intersection.
questions.explanation: A yellow light means a red light is coming soon. Stop unless you are already in the intersection.

questions.question: Before you start the engine, you should:

options.text: Make sure only back seat passengers have buckled their seat belts.
Make sure only adult passengers have buckled their seat belts.
Make sure only child passengers have buckled their seat belts.
Make sure all passengers have buckled their seat belts.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make sure all passengers have buckled their seat belts.
questions.explanation: Before you start the engine, buckle your seat belt. Then check that all passengers have buckled theirs too. Make this a habit every time you drive.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: A crossroad is ahead. Watch for other traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: A crossroad is ahead. Watch for other traffic.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that a crossroad is coming ahead.

questions.question: Driving too fast:

options.text: Saves time and gets you to your destination faster.
Increases the chance of serious injury or death.

questions.correctAnswerText: Increases the chance of serious injury or death.
questions.explanation: Driving too fast is a major cause of car crashes. It does not save time and leads to poor driving choices.

questions.question: Check your blind spot by looking over your shoulder when:

options.text: Pulling toward or away from a curb.

questions.explanation: Check your blind spot every time you move your vehicle. This includes turning, changing lanes, and pulling toward or away from a curb.

questions.question: Which statement is true about seat belts and child restraints?

options.text: Never put an infant or small child in the front seat of a vehicle with airbags.
An airbag can hurt an infant or small child, even in a low-speed crash.
Always make sure all passengers use a seat belt or child restraint.

questions.explanation: Before you drive, fasten your seat belt and make sure all passengers use seat belts or child restraints. Seat belts greatly reduce the chance of injury or death in a crash. Children 12 and under must sit in a rear seat with proper restraints. Never put a rear-facing infant car seat in the front seat of a vehicle with a front airbag.

questions.question: Which of these substances can affect your ability to drive?

options.text: Cough syrup and cold tablets with codeine or antihistamines.

questions.explanation: Many drugs can impair your driving. These include tranquilizers, sedatives, over-the-counter cough syrups, cold tablets, allergy medicines with alcohol or antihistamines, and illegal drugs.

questions.question: When you see a stopped school bus with flashing lights and an extended signal arm, you should:

options.text: Drive at 15 mph if no children are visible.
Drive at normal speed but watch for children.

questions.explanation: You must come to a complete stop when you see a school bus with flashing lights and an extended signal arm. Stay stopped until the signal arm goes down and the bus starts moving again. This applies whether you are driving in the same direction or the opposite direction.

questions.question: You should always follow directions given by a school crossing guard.
questions.explanation: Always follow directions from a crossing guard or law enforcement officer. Reduce your speed and use caution in school zones.

questions.question: An orange and red triangle on the back of a vehicle means:
questions.explanation: Slow-moving vehicles such as farm tractors, road maintenance vehicles, and animal-drawn carts display an orange and red triangle on the back.

questions.question: The most common mistake drivers make when backing up is failing to look both ways behind them.
questions.explanation: When backing up, many drivers fail to look both ways behind them. Mirrors do not show everything. Turn your body and head to look through the rear window to see as much as possible.

questions.question: What should you do if you meet an aggressive driver?
questions.explanation: The safest choice is to get out of an aggressive driver's way. Do not try to compete with other drivers. Always follow the rules to keep everyone safe.

questions.question: When backing up, what should you do?

options.text: Drive much more slowly than usual.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive much more slowly than usual.
questions.explanation: Your car is harder to control when backing up. Back up slowly—no faster than a walking pace.

questions.question: When driving in fog, which headlights should you use?
questions.explanation: Use low beam headlights in fog, rain, or snow. High beams reflect off moisture and make it harder to see.

questions.question: When is it important to slow down?

options.text: When the road is wet or slippery.

questions.explanation: Slow down on narrow or winding roads, at intersections, at railroad crossings, on hills, in sharp curves, where there are pedestrians or hazards, and when roads are wet or slippery.

questions.question: Like alcohol and drugs, drowsiness can:

options.text: Help you be a better driver.

questions.explanation: Lack of sleep causes poor driving. Drowsiness slows your reaction time, reduces awareness, and damages judgment—just like alcohol and drugs do.

questions.question: Why should you not follow other cars too closely?

options.text: You may not see the road between the cars.
You may not have time to stop if the car in front slows or stops suddenly.
You may not see the car's turn signals.
You may not see the car's brake lights.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may not have time to stop if the car in front slows or stops suddenly.
questions.explanation: If you follow too closely, you won't have enough time to stop if the car ahead stops suddenly. This can cause a crash.

questions.question: Which substances can impair your driving and lead to a DUI arrest?
questions.explanation: Many substances can impair your driving. These include alcohol, illegal drugs, inhalants, and many legal medicines (prescription and over-the-counter).

questions.question: You should not pass another vehicle if you don't have space to return to your lane.
questions.explanation: Do not pass unless you have enough space to safely return to your lane. Don't assume you have time to pass multiple cars or that other drivers will make room for you.

questions.question: Where should drivers not pass other vehicles?
questions.explanation: Do not pass at intersections, crossroads, railroad crossings, or business entrances. Passing is dangerous because your view is blocked by the car you are passing. Trains or other vehicles may enter.

questions.question: What should you do at a school crossing sign?

options.text: Always stop, even without a stop sign.
Watch for children and be ready to stop.
Always honk your horn when you see children.
Be ready to help children cross the street.

questions.correctAnswerText: Watch for children and be ready to stop.
questions.explanation: Always yield to pedestrians in or entering a crosswalk. Watch for pedestrians at intersections and when turning.

questions.question: What can cause distracted driving?

options.text: Talking or texting on a cell phone.
Changing a radio station or CD.

questions.explanation: Drivers make about 200 decisions for every mile they drive. You must focus fully on driving. Any extra task can be dangerous.

questions.question: When the road is wet or icy, you should:
questions.explanation: Your tires grip wet, snowy, or icy roads less than dry roads. Slow down when the road is wet or icy.

questions.question: When a school bus ahead on your side has red lights flashing, you must:

options.text: Slow to a speed no faster than 10 mph.
Stop until the lights stop flashing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop until the lights stop flashing.
questions.explanation: When a school bus has flashing red lights, it is loading or unloading students. Do not move until the red lights stop flashing and the stop arm goes up. Never pass a school bus that is picking up or dropping off students.

questions.question: Yellow pavement markings show that traffic is moving in opposite directions.
questions.explanation: White lines separate traffic going the same direction. Yellow lines separate traffic going opposite directions.

questions.question: A sign of a drunk driver is:
questions.explanation: Signs of drunk driving include speeding, weaving, driving slower than traffic, jerky movements, and sudden stops.

questions.question: At a stop sign with no crosswalk, you must stop before entering the intersection.
questions.explanation: At a stop sign, stop at the stop line if there is one. If no stop line, stop before the crosswalk. If no crosswalk, stop before entering the intersection.

questions.question: You see pedestrians near the road. You should:

options.text: Speed up to get past them quickly.
Slow down and pass with caution.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and pass with caution.
questions.explanation: Watch for pedestrians who may cross your path. If you see pedestrians near the road, slow down and be ready to stop if needed.

questions.question: This sign shows a railroad crossing with no signal. You should:

options.text: Keep a steady speed while looking and listening for trains.
Slow down, look both ways, listen for trains, and be ready to stop if needed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down, look both ways, listen for trains, and be ready to stop if needed.
questions.explanation: At this railroad crossing, slow down, look both ways, and listen for trains. Be ready to stop if a train is near. Never try to race a train.

questions.question: A school bus is stopped on the opposite side of a divided highway. You:

options.text: Must stop and wait for the flashing lights to stop.
Must stop until the school bus moves.
Must stop until the stop arm is lifted.

questions.explanation: If a school bus is stopped on the opposite side of a divided highway, you may continue. If the highway has no median, drivers on both sides must stop.

questions.question: A steady green traffic light means:

options.text: You may go through the intersection at a safe speed if it is clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may go through the intersection at a safe speed if it is clear.
questions.explanation: A green light means you can go through the intersection. Let any traffic or pedestrians already in the intersection pass first, then go when it is safe.

questions.question: Why is using a cell phone while driving considered a distraction?

options.text: It makes the driver worry about the cost of the call.
It takes up the driver's hands, eyes, and mind.
It draws the attention of other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: It takes up the driver's hands, eyes, and mind.
questions.explanation: Using a cell phone while driving is dangerous because it uses your eyes, hands, and mind. Even skilled drivers increase their risk of a crash when using a cell phone on the road.

questions.question: What can happen if you take a prescription drug and drink alcohol together?

options.text: There will likely be no effect.
It will make you more alert.
It can make you unsafe to drive.

questions.correctAnswerText: It can make you unsafe to drive.
questions.explanation: Prescription and over-the-counter medications can reduce your ability to drive safely. They are especially dangerous when mixed with alcohol.

questions.question: Drivers should keep a safe distance from cyclists.
questions.explanation: Drivers must be careful around cyclists and keep a safe distance between their vehicle and the cyclist.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: You must travel at the speed shown.
The highest legal speed on this road is 55 mph.
You must travel through the intersection at the posted speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: The highest legal speed on this road is 55 mph.
questions.explanation: This is a speed limit sign. It shows the highest legal speed you can drive on that road. In bad weather like rain, snow, or ice, you may need to drive slower than the posted limit.

questions.question: When you turn left at an intersection:

options.text: You must yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.
Oncoming traffic and pedestrians must yield to you.
You never need to yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.
questions.explanation: Drivers turning left must yield to oncoming traffic going straight. Drivers must always yield to pedestrians.

questions.question: What does alcohol cause?
questions.explanation: Even a small amount of alcohol reduces your vision, judgment, concentration, and coordination.

questions.question: Only vehicles with special plates or parking placards for people with disabilities can park in disability spaces.
questions.explanation: A parking space marked "Reserved Parking for Persons with Disabilities" can only be used by vehicles with disability license plates, Disabled Veteran license plates, or disability parking placards.

questions.question: What does a red and white triangular sign at an intersection mean?

options.text: Slow down if an emergency vehicle is near.
Look both ways as you cross the intersection.
Always stop completely at the intersection.
Slow down and be ready to stop if needed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and be ready to stop if needed.
questions.explanation: A red and white triangular yield sign means you must slow down as you approach the intersection and let other vehicles or pedestrians go first. Be prepared to stop if necessary.

questions.question: Before you start the engine, you should:

options.text: Make sure all passengers have buckled their safety belts.

questions.explanation: Create a routine when getting in and out of your car. Before starting the engine, buckle your safety belt and make sure all passengers do the same.

questions.question: If there is no sign or marking that prevents passing, it is safe to pass.
questions.explanation: Signs and lane markings show where it is unsafe to pass. You must decide if it is safe to pass in other areas.
